intended_object: The equivalence of categories ContAction V H ≌ ContAction V G between continuous actions of H and of G, given by restricting scalars along an isomorphism of topological monoids f : G ≃ₜ* H (from the docstring). It is the continuous version of Action.resEquiv.
explanation: The functor restricts along f and the inverse restricts along f.symm. The unit and counit are natural isomorphisms built from `resCongr` and `resComp`, using f.symm ∘ f = id and f ∘ f.symm = id. This is exactly the standard equivalence that restriction of scalars along an isomorphism induces. The setting is already as general as the file allows: any monoid with a topology, and any concrete category V that has a forgetful functor to TopCat. A topological-monoid isomorphism is the natural input, because a continuous inverse is needed for the inverse functor to preserve continuity of actions. The discrete analogue `Action.resEquiv` (if present) is a different object, because it works on all of Action V G rather than on the full subcategory of continuous actions. So Mathlib has no other definition of this same equivalence.
